APIKeyAuthenticationModel.description:
API key authentication.

Used by: Generic REST APIs, some cloud services. All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

api_key.description: Key reference for API key value

api_secret.description: Key reference for API secret (used alongside the API key)

endpoint.description: Key reference for API endpoint URL

header_name.description: Key reference for HTTP header name (default: 'X-API-Key')

AWSAuthenticationModel.description:
AWS access key authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

access_key_id.description: Key reference for AWS access key ID

secret_access_key.description: Key reference for AWS secret access key

session_token.description: Key reference for AWS session token (temporary credentials)

role_arn.description: Key reference for AWS IAM role ARN for AssumeRole

AuthenticationModel.description:
How to authenticate to a cloud provider or an integration. `method` selects the scheme and the block of the same name holds its settings.

Credential fields are key references: the names of variables or secrets declared in an Environment, resolved when they are needed. Never put a credential value here.

Rules:
- The block named by `method` must be set (for example `method: oauth2` needs `oauth2`).
- No other method's block may be set at the same time.

ssh_key.description: SSH private key authentication (git deploy keys)

description.description: Human-readable description of this authentication configuration and setup instructions

CLIAuthenticationModel.description:
CLI-based authentication using local credentials.

Uses existing CLI authentication: az login, gcloud auth, aws configure. No credential references needed - uses ambient credentials.

use_cli.description: Use local CLI authentication (az, gcloud, aws)

CertificateAuthenticationModel.description:
Certificate-based authentication (mTLS).

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

certificate_path.description: Key reference for client certificate file path

private_key_path.description: Key reference for private key file path

ca_bundle_path.description: Key reference for CA bundle file path

certificate_password.description: Key reference for certificate password (if encrypted)

CommonLifecycleModel.description:
Lifecycle phases for common models.

Maps phase names to phase configurations. Phase names follow the pattern ``{command}_{action}_{suffix}``, e.g. ``deploy_plan_before``, ``deploy_provision``, ``deploy_destroy_after``, ``config_clear``. This is an open map (any phase name is allowed) rather than a fixed set of fields, since each kind and provisioner type defines its own set of supported phases.

CommonLifecyclePhaseModel.description: Lifecycle phase configuration: a description plus its scripts.

scripts.description: Scripts to run. Each entry is a path relative to the solution root, with one of the extensions bash, go, js, mjs, ps1, py, sh, or an object with `file`, `scope`, `priority` and `target`.

GCPAuthenticationModel.description:
Google Cloud Platform service account authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

project_id.description: Key reference for GCP project ID

credentials_json.description: Key reference for GCP service account JSON credentials (as string content)

credentials_file.description: Key reference for path to GCP service account JSON file

service_account_email.description: Key reference for GCP service account email

ManagedIdentityAuthenticationModel.description:
Managed/Workload Identity authentication.

Uses cloud provider managed identity (Azure MSI, GCP Workload Identity, AWS IAM Roles). No credential references needed - uses ambient credentials.

client_id.description: Key reference for user-assigned managed identity client ID (Azure only)

OAuth2AuthenticationModel.description:
OAuth2/OpenID Connect authentication.

Used by: Azure (Service Principal), generic OAuth2 providers. All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

client_id.description: Key reference for OAuth2 client/application ID

client_secret.description: Key reference for OAuth2 client secret

tenant_id.description: Key reference for tenant/directory ID (Azure AD, Okta, etc.)

token_url.description: Key reference for OAuth2 token endpoint URL

authorization_url.description: Key reference for OAuth2 authorization endpoint URL

ProviderMetaModel.description: Provider metadata including name, annotations, labels, and tags.

tags.description: Optional tags (list of values for categorization)

ProviderSpecModel.description: A cloud or infrastructure account: its provider `type`, primary `region`, how to authenticate, and optional free-form settings and default tags.

lifecycle.description: Hook scripts per phase name, for example `deploy_plan_before` or `deploy_destroy_after`. Accepted and validated, but strata does not run lifecycle hooks yet.

type.description: Provider type, for example `azure` or `kamatera`. Must be listed in the Configuration's `spec.providers`, and is matched to the ProviderConfig document of that name.

region.description: Primary region or datacenter of this account, for example `westeurope`. Must be one of the regions in the ProviderConfig of this `type`, unless that ProviderConfig allows additional regions. It is strata's own identifier, not necessarily an argument of the Terraform provider block; the region's geography comes from the ProviderConfig.

display_name.description: Optional human-readable label for the region (e.g., 'West US', 'eu-west-1'). Purely cosmetic/documentation — not a distinct geographic concept from `region` and not required for provider validation.

authentication.description:
Authentication configuration for cloud provider access

Rules:
- The block named by `method` must be set (for example `method: oauth2` needs `oauth2`).
- No other method's block may be set at the same time.

configuration.description: Free-form provisioner settings (for example extra Terraform provider-block arguments such as `skip_provider_registration`), passed to Terraform as `strata.providers.<slot>.configuration`. Strata does not validate the keys itself: add an `attributeconfig` with `target.kind: provider` and `target.block: configuration` to do so.

custom.description: Free-form key/value pairs for your own scripts and Terraform code (for example cost center or billing account), passed to Terraform as `strata.providers.<slot>.custom`. Strata does not interpret them. Validate them with an `attributeconfig` targeting `provider` and `custom`.

default_tags.description: Default cloud tags for everything created through this provider, passed to Terraform as `strata.providers.<slot>.default_tags`. Not the same as `meta.tags`, which is a free-form list for documentation. Strata does not limit the number of tags, so stay within your cloud provider's limit.

SAMLAuthenticationModel.description:
SAML 2.0 authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

idp_entity_id.description: Key reference for SAML Identity Provider entity ID

sp_entity_id.description: Key reference for SAML Service Provider entity ID

sso_url.description: Key reference for SAML Single Sign-On URL

certificate_path.description: Key reference for SAML certificate file path

SSHKeyAuthenticationModel.description: SSH private key authentication, used for git deploy keys. Every field is a key reference, never the key itself.

private_key.description: Key reference for the SSH private key (PEM/OpenSSH format)

passphrase.description: Key reference for the private key's passphrase, if encrypted

known_hosts.description: Key reference for a known_hosts entry pinning the remote host's key

ScriptPathModel.description: Individual script with scope and execution metadata.

scope.description: Execution scope - determines how many times the script runs (e.g. deployment, environment, workspace, provider, resource, module, namespace)

priority.description: Execution order within scope (lower runs first)

TokenAuthenticationModel.description: Bearer or personal access token authentication, used for git over HTTPS. `token` is a key reference; `username` is a literal.

token.description: Key reference for the token/PAT value

username.description: Literal username to pair with the token — not a key reference

description: A cloud or infrastructure account, for example one Azure subscription: its provider type, primary region and credentials. Create one per account. A workspace uses providers through named slots, which a deployment can rebind to another provider.
